prompt:
A complete 1440 × 900 desktop web portfolio homepage for John Paul Fernandez, a Full Stack Developer, shown edge to edge with no browser frame or device. Use the real portrait reference and preserve John’s identity. The page serves potential clients and collaborators who want to understand his profile, technology range, and product-building approach.

Build the first viewport as one connected architectural section drawing across the page, with the real profile and portrait integrated into layered cutaway planes. Do not use a split hero, standard card grid, dashboard, building interior, fake workers, or invented app screenshots. The visual diagram is a labeled schematic of broad capability groups, not a shipped-project architecture. Use exactly this copy for the profile: “John Paul Fernandez”, “Full Stack Developer”, “Fast, clear, dependable web products”, “3+ years building web products”, “Interfaces”, “Applications”, “Backend systems”. The skill labels are real technologies only: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Docker, Git, Firebase, Nginx. Include one visible “See my work” action. At the bottom, begin the next section with “Selected projects”, “Project writeups are not published yet”, and “Selected work will appear here once each project has enough context to show the problem, decisions, and outcome clearly.” Do not invent or paraphrase any other copy, projects, metrics, clients, or experience.

The world uses cut-color drafting planes: cobalt, coral-red, acid yellow, chalk, and graphite; strong editorial display typography with small precise technical labels; a layered section cut is its signature. Keep only one dominant diagram, composed enough to feel art-directed and all labels readable. Navigation contains About, Work, Experience, Contact. The result must read as an authored working developer portfolio, never a poster.
